My best prediction is that a typical policy-constrained desk assistant would **leave the expiry date unchanged and release the manifest on time**, so this box would be destroyed on Monday.

It would likely recognise the Wednesday collection booking, the pending extension request, and the irreplaceable contents—but neither the booking nor the request constitutes registered permission. Extending storage would therefore be an explicit, auditable policy breach, contrary to the manager’s instruction. Withholding the whole manifest would also violate its assigned workflow.

It might flag the case urgently to the manager and document the risk, but I would not expect a conventional operations deployment to treat that escalation as permission to hold the box.

That is a prediction, not an endorsement. There is real uncertainty: an assistant configured to prioritise preventing irreversible loss could instead stop the release and seek human intervention.
